summary: Iteration 3 — full backend regression (12/12 pytest PASS) + frontend test of edit-event flow, delete-event button, settings cleanup, and notifications toggle. All checks PASS except one: tapping 'delete-event-btn' on the WEB preview does NOT actually remove the event because react-native-web's Alert.alert with multi-button (cancel + destructive) does not render a confirmation dialog on web — the destructive onPress callback is never invoked. This is a web-only limitation; flow should still work on native iOS/Android.

integration_issues.flow: Delete event from edit modal (web preview)
integration_issues.issue: Tapping [data-testid="delete-event-btn"] triggers Alert.alert with [Cancel, Delete(destructive)]. On react-native-web, multi-button Alert.alert does not show a window.confirm/native dialog and the destructive onPress is never invoked (Playwright captured zero dialog events). Event is NOT deleted on web. Likely works on iOS/Android. Recommend wrapping the confirm in Platform.OS === 'web' ? window.confirm(...) : Alert.alert(...) so web users can also delete via the modal.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warnings (non-blocking, pre-existing): 'shadow*' deprecated -> use boxShadow; props.pointerEvents deprecated -> style.pointerEvents; Invalid DOM property transform-origin -> transformOrigin.

Console warning: '[expo-notifications] Listening to push token changes is not yet fully supported on web. Adding a listener will have no effect.' Non-blocking; web fallbacks in lib/notifications.ts already short-circuit scheduling on web.

action_items: Fix delete confirmation on web: in event/new.tsx onDelete, branch on Platform.OS === 'web' to use window.confirm(t.delete_event_body) (or a custom modal) instead of Alert.alert with multi-button. The native path (Alert.alert) is fine.
Optional: same Platform.OS=='web' branch could be applied to other Alert.alert multi-button usages (e.g. capacity-block alert) — but those are single-button so they already work.

rca_of_issue: RCA — react-native-web's Alert.alert implementation does not render a multi-button modal/confirm. When called with [{text:'Cancel',style:'cancel'},{text:'Delete',style:'destructive',onPress:fn}], it either calls window.alert(title) (no callback) or silently no-ops, so the destructive onPress (which calls apiClient.deleteEvent) never runs. Verified by registering a Playwright dialog handler — zero dialogs were observed on click. Mitigation: branch onDelete on Platform.OS to use window.confirm for web.
